config.title: Simple Todo List

intro.title: Simple Todo List
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple todo list application where you can add new tasks, mark them as completed, and remove them from the list. You'll learn how to use Angular components to structure your UI and manage data with TypeScript. The core programming concepts involved are component creation, data binding, and event handling to make your app interactive. By the end, you'll have a functional todo list that demonstrates fundamental Angular development.
intro.usecase: Todo list patterns are fundamental building blocks in countless real-world applications. You'll see this same pattern in project management tools like Asana or Trello where users add and track tasks, in e-commerce checkout flows where shoppers manage items in their cart, and in content management systems where editors maintain lists of articles or media. As a developer, you'll implement similar list management functionality for user dashboards, admin panels, notification centers, and any interface requiring dynamic item collection and status tracking. Mastering this pattern gives you the foundation to build interactive data-driven components across web and mobile applications.

objectives: Construct a component class with properties to manage todo items
Initialize and manipulate an array to store todo data
Implement a method to add new items to the todo list
Configure event binding to handle user input for adding todos
Render the todo list dynamically using Angular's template syntax
Apply structural directives to display conditional content
Integrate a form control to capture and clear user input

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from @angular/core and @angular/common
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common' in your TypeScript file.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbol name and the module path in quotes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular modules are imported to create a component and use template directives.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both Component and CommonModule from their correct module paths.
steps.feedbackWrong: import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.

steps.title: Create the TodoListComponent class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript class named TodoListComponent and decorate it with @Component. Inside the decorator, provide the configuration: selector: 'app-todo-list', templateUrl: './todo-list.component.html', and standalone: true.
steps.hint: Remember to export the class so it can be used elsewhere in the application.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Create TodoListComponent class with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: A TodoListComponent class is defined with the @Component decorator containing the required metadata.
successCriteria: TodoListComponent class is created, exported, and decorated with @Component containing selector, templateUrl, and standalone: true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your class is named TodoListComponent, exported, and includes all three properties (selector, templateUrl, standalone: true) in the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you have a class named TodoListComponent, it's exported, and the @Component decorator contains selector, templateUrl, and standalone: true.

steps.title: Define Todo interface for type safety
steps.instruction: Inside the TodoListComponent class file, above the @Component decorator, define a TypeScript interface named Todo with three properties: id (number), text (string), and completed (boolean).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Todo interface is defined with proper TypeScript type annotations for all three required properties.
successCriteria: Todo interface exists with id: number, text: string, and completed: boolean properties
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that all three properties (id, text, completed) have the correct TypeScript types (number, string, boolean).
steps.feedbackWrong: The Todo interface needs to be defined with all three properties and their types. Try using: interface Todo { id: number; text: string; completed: boolean; }

steps.title: Initialize todos array with sample data
steps.instruction: Inside the TodoListComponent class, create a property named 'todos' with type Todo[] and initialize it with 2-3 sample todo items.
steps.hint: Define the property as 'todos: Todo[] = [...]' and include sample objects with 'id', 'text', and 'completed' properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a typed todos array containing sample todo items ready for display.
successCriteria: The todos property is defined as Todo[] with at least two sample todo objects containing id, text, and completed properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure todos is typed as Todo[] and contains at least two sample objects with id, text, and completed properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The todos property isn't properly initialized. It should be a Todo[] array with sample todo objects.

steps.title: Add newTodoText property for input binding
steps.instruction: In the TodoListComponent class, add a property named newTodoText of type string and initialize it to an empty string.
steps.hint: This property will store the text entered in the input field for adding new todos.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a reactive property to bind to the todo input field.
successCriteria: The TodoListComponent class contains a newTodoText property of type string initialized to an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but check that it's named exactly 'newTodoText', has type 'string', and is initialized to an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The property is missing or incorrect. Add 'newTodoText: string = '';' inside the TodoListComponent class.

steps.title: Create addTodo method to add new todos
steps.instruction: In the TodoListComponent class, create a method named addTodo that adds a new todo to the todos array and clears the newTodoText property.
steps.hint: The method should create a new Todo object with a unique id, the text from newTodoText, and completed set to false, then push it to the todos array and reset newTodoText to an empty string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an addTodo method that can be called to add new todos to the list.
successCriteria: The addTodo method is defined in the TodoListComponent class, creates a new Todo object with the correct properties, pushes it to the todos array, and clears newTodoText.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your method creates a complete Todo object with id, text, and completed properties, adds it to the todos array, and clears newTodoText.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addTodo method isn't quite right. Remember to create a new Todo object with a unique id (you can use Date.now()), the text from newTodoText, completed set to false, then push it to the todos array and reset newTodoText to an empty string.

steps.title: Add input field for new todo text
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add an input element with two-way data binding to the newTodoText property using [(ngModel)]. Include a placeholder attribute with the text 'Add a new todo'.
steps.hint: Use Angular's ngModel directive for two-way binding. Remember to import FormsModule if you haven't already (though it's already in CommonModule for standalone components).
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example: input with two-way binding -->
<input type="text" [(ngModel)]="taskName" placeholder="Enter task name" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains an input field that binds to newTodoText, allowing users to type new todo items.
successCriteria: The input element uses [(ngModel)]="newTodoText" and has a placeholder attribute with the text 'Add a new todo'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the input has both [(ngModel)] binding to newTodoText and a placeholder attribute with the text 'Add a new todo'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field is missing or incomplete. Check that you've added an input element with [(ngModel)]="newTodoText" and placeholder='Add a new todo'.

steps.title: Add button to submit new todo and wire click event
steps.instruction: Add a button element after the input field in the template. Bind its (click) event to the addTodo method and add a [disabled] attribute that disables the button when newTodoText is empty.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click) and property binding [disabled] with a condition checking if newTodoText is empty.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example button with event and property binding
<button (click)="submitForm()" [disabled]="!isValid">Submit</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears next to the input field that adds a new todo when clicked and is disabled when the input is empty.
successCriteria: Button element is added with (click)="addTodo()" and [disabled]="!newTodoText.trim()" attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but it's missing either the click event binding or the disabled property binding. Make sure to include both (click)="addTodo()" and [disabled]="!newTodoText.trim()".
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is not properly configured. Check that you've added the button element with both event and property bindings as specified.

steps.title: Display todos list with *ngFor directive
steps.instruction: Add a <ul> element after the button that uses *ngFor to iterate over the todos array and display each todo as an <li>.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor="let todo of todos" on the <li> element. Inside the <li>, display todo.text.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: rendering a list with *ngFor
  • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The todos array is displayed as a list of items in the UI.
successCriteria: A <ul> element with <li> items using *ngFor to iterate over todos is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added the <ul> and <li> elements with *ngFor.
steps.feedbackWrong: The todo list isn't displaying. Check that you've added the <ul> and <li> with *ngFor.

steps.title: Add complete toggle and delete buttons for each todo
steps.instruction: Inside the existing *ngFor loop, add a checkbox with (change) event bound to toggleTodo(todo.id) and a button with (click) event bound to deleteTodo(todo.id) for each todo item.
steps.hint: Add the checkbox and button elements within the same list item container as the todo text. Use todo.id as the parameter for both event handlers.
steps.analogousExample: • {{ item.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: Each todo item in the list will have a checkbox to toggle completion status and a delete button to remove it.
successCriteria: Checkbox with (change)="toggleTodo(todo.id)" and button with (click)="deleteTodo(todo.id)" are added inside the *ngFor loop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some controls, but make sure both the checkbox with (change) event and delete button with (click) event are present for each todo item.
steps.feedbackWrong: The controls aren't properly added. Each todo item needs a checkbox with (change)="toggleTodo(todo.id)" and a button with (click)="deleteTodo(todo.id)" inside the *ngFor loop.
